    \quad person (PRS)           & \crd{9}$-0.35$* & \crd{8}$-0.33$* & \cg{1}$+0.04$ & \crd{3}$-0.11$* & \crd{3}$-0.10$* & \crd{0}$-0.01$* \\

    \bottomrule
  \end{tabular}
  \caption{Paired differences between human-written and GPT-5.2--generated
  Swedish text (Cohen's $d_z$, LLM $-$ human; paired Wilcoxon signed-rank with
  Benjamini--Hochberg FDR correction). Positive (green) values indicate higher
  feature values in LLM text; negative (red) values indicate higher values in
  human text; shading intensity is proportional to $|d_z|$. * denotes
  significance at $q<0.05$. A representative subset of the full feature set is
  shown, selecting one feature per redundant construct family; full results in
  Appendix~\ref{app:full-features}. An em-dash marks a feature not reported
  for that register. Formal: $n=170$ pairs; informal: $n=1{,}149$
  pairs (informal MTLD: $n=963$, MTLD is undefined for the shortest comments). Note that at informal $n$ the star is close to uninformative
  --- 38 of 46 features clear $q<0.05$ at baseline --- so the effect
  size, not the star, is what distinguishes these rows.}
  \label{tab:features-gpt}
\end{table}

  \caption{Complete informal feature set: paired differences between
  human-written and GPT-5.2--generated Swedish (Cohen's $d_z$, LLM $-$ human;
  paired Wilcoxon signed-rank, Benjamini--Hochberg FDR within each condition's
  family of 46 features). Positive (green) values indicate higher feature
  values in LLM text, negative (red) higher in human text; shading is proportional
  to $|d_z|$. * denotes $q<0.05$. Medians are from the baseline condition.
  Features are grouped by extractor and ordered by $|d_z|$ at baseline; names are
  the raw column names in
  \texttt{significance\_tests\_results.csv}. All features have $n=1{,}149$ pairs except \texttt{mtld} $n=963$, which is undefined for the shortest texts. Significant features per
  condition: Baseline 38/46, Human-like 39/46, Detector-evasive 38/46 --- at this $n$ the star is close to uninformative, so
  $|d_z|$ is what distinguishes rows. Note that \texttt{\_count} features scale
  with length and \texttt{\_rate} features do not, so the two disagree by
  construction wherever the LLM writes longer text.}
  \label{app:full-features}
\end{table}

  \caption{Complete formal feature set: paired differences between
  human-written and GPT-5.2--generated Swedish (Cohen's $d_z$, LLM $-$ human;
  paired Wilcoxon signed-rank, Benjamini--Hochberg FDR within each condition's
  family of 39 features). Positive (green) values indicate higher feature
  values in LLM text, negative (red) higher in human text; shading is proportional
  to $|d_z|$. * denotes $q<0.05$. Medians are from the baseline condition.
  Features are grouped by extractor and ordered by $|d_z|$ at baseline; names are
  the raw column names in
  \texttt{significance\_tests\_results.csv}. Significant features per
  condition: Baseline 29/39, Human-like 32/39, Detector-evasive 25/39 --- at this $n$ the star is close to uninformative, so
  $|d_z|$ is what distinguishes rows. Note that \texttt{\_count} features scale
  with length and \texttt{\_rate} features do not, so the two disagree by
  construction wherever the LLM writes longer text.}
  \label{app:full-features-formal}
\end{table}

% ---- Embedding detectability ----
\begin{table}[htbp]
  \centering
  \caption{Human--LLM separability by prompt condition: cross-validated ROC AUC
  of a logistic-regression two-sample test on multilingual sentence embeddings
  (\texttt{paraphrase-multilingual-mpnet-base-v2}, 5-fold CV, 1000 label
  permutations), and mean per-pair cosine similarity. AUC${}=0.5$ is chance;
  all conditions separate at permutation $p<0.001$.
  $n=170$ (formal) / $1{,}149$ (informal) pairs per class.}
  \label{tab:embedding-detectability}

    \cmidrule(lr){2-3}\cmidrule(lr){4-5}
    Condition & ROC AUC & Mean cos. & ROC AUC & Mean cos. \\
    \midrule
    Baseline                   & 0.754 & 0.775 & 0.960 & 0.477 \\
    Human-like                 & 0.764 & 0.760 & 0.963 & 0.479 \\
    Detector-evasive           & 0.880 & 0.749 & 0.981 & 0.479 \\
    \bottomrule
  \end{tabular}
\end{table}

% ---- Feature-based detector ----
\begin{table}[htbp]
  \centering
  \caption{Feature-based (non-LLM) detector: a balanced logistic regression
  trained on the handcrafted linguistic features alone
  (39 formal / 46 informal features from syntactic complexity,
  stylometric surface, pragmatic markers and NER), scored by 5-fold
  cross-validation. Folds are grouped so that both halves of a pair --- and, in
  the informal register, every comment from the same thread --- stay in one
  fold, so the scores cannot be inflated by topic leakage.
  AUC${}=0.5$ is chance; every cell separates at $p<0.001$ (1000 label
  permutations). $n=170$ formal / $n=963$ informal documents per class
  (informal drops 186 of the 1{,}149 pairs for missing feature values).
  Stratified (ungrouped) CV gives near-identical AUCs, formal/informal:
  Baseline 0.9991/0.9781; Human-like 0.9991/0.9777; Detector-evasive 0.9962/0.9921.
  Contrast with Table~\ref{tab:embedding-detectability}: the interpretable
  feature detector separates human from LLM text better than the embedding
  two-sample test in every condition and both registers. Prompt-based evasion
  does not defeat it --- in the informal register the detector-evasive prompt
  makes text \emph{more} detectable (0.9755 $\to$ 0.9928), and in the
  formal register it barely dents an already near-ceiling score
  (0.9995 $\to$ 0.9978).}
  \label{tab:feature-detector}
  \begin{tabular}{lcccccccc}
    \toprule
    & \multicolumn{4}{c}{Formal} & \multicolumn{4}{c}{Informal} \\
    \cmidrule(lr){2-5}\cmidrule(lr){6-9}
    Condition & ROC AUC & SD & Acc. & $F_1$ & ROC AUC & SD & Acc. & $F_1$ \\
    \midrule
    Baseline           & 0.9995 & 0.0007 & 0.985 & 0.985 & 0.9755 & 0.0091 & 0.930 & 0.935 \\
    Human-like         & 0.9995 & 0.0010 & 0.988 & 0.989 & 0.9740 & 0.0087 & 0.928 & 0.933 \\
    Detector-evasive   & 0.9978 & 0.0022 & 0.979 & 0.979 & 0.9928 & 0.0028 & 0.954 & 0.957 \\
    \bottomrule
  \end{tabular}
\end{table}
